newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle brisk at $69, up $1 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle brisk at $69, up $1 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday sold at $69.00 per cwt in active trading, supported by continued steep gains in beef prices, feedlot sources said.
Sales at $69.00 were $1.00 higher from Tuesday and $3.00 higher from last week's top.
Trading was brisk, with most of the remainder of this week's showlists sold, the feedlot sources said.

An estimated 60,700 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, which brought the week to date figure to 110,500, including 20,900 formulated cattle to be shipped this week, USDA said.

Kansas sales were pegged at 32,300 head, USDA said. The sales brought the week to date figure to 79,700 head including 14,600 or about 18 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA said.

Beef prices Wednesday were quoted up $1.97 to $2.21 per cwt, with 261 fabricated loads sold, USDA said. Heavy weight choice was quoted up $2.21 at $104.62, up $8.11 from the same period a week ago, USDA statistics showed.
Fed cattle prices next week were seen trading up $1.00 at $70.00 amid expectations for continued strong beef prices, sources said.
Prices also were seen buoyed by estimates next week for smaller showlists and tighter supplies of finished cattle.
